chronologicaltimeline.title: Staff notation through the centuries

events.title: Neumes
events.detail: Earliest written notation, squiggles above text hinting at melodic contour, no pitch precision.

events.title: Guido of Arezzo
events.detail: Invented the four-line staff and the sol-fa syllable system (ut re mi fa sol la). First reliably readable pitch notation.

events.title: Mensural notation
events.detail: Rhythm encoded for the first time via note shapes, unlocks polyphony (multiple independent voices).

events.title: Music printing press
events.detail: Ottaviano Petrucci's moveable-type music printing spreads sheet music across Europe.

events.title: Baroque conventions
events.detail: Five-line treble and bass staves standardised; figured bass shorthand speeds up harmonisation.

events.title: Modern score
events.detail: Dynamics (pp→ff), articulation, and expression marks codified; engraving produces the notation we use today.

chronologicaltimeline.footer: Western notation is ~1,000 years old. Non-Western traditions (Indian raga, Arabic maqam, Chinese gongche) use entirely different systems.
